construct: per-COLUMN text alignment - the label cell `text-align: left`, the numeric cell `text-align: right`, at fixed column widths
why: Right-aligned numerics are the difference between a table and a list of words. The alignment lives on the CELL, is different per column, and is the only thing that makes the two rows' digits line up on their last character - a fact a grader can check with a ruler and no knowledge of the source.

canvas.note: textAlignHorizontal RIGHT on the numeric cell's text node

mustHave: the two rows' numeric values ('7' and '128') are right-aligned with each other - their right edges match
the two label values ('Widget', 'Gadget') are left-aligned with each other
the numeric column and the label column do not overlap
the numeric column sits to the right of the label column in both rows

predictedWall.status: EXISTING - cited as the governing lowering, NOT as a predicted failure
predictedWall.why: spec/lowering.json registers this rule as 'text hugs unless hugging would move it' - it asks whether the packing agrees with the text alignment and keeps the glyphs where CSS put them. A right-aligned numeric cell at a FIXED column width is precisely the shape where hugging WOULD move the text, so this rule should fire and keep the alignment. I am naming it so that if the digits come back left-aligned, the first place to look is this rule failing to fire rather than text-align being unread. Predicted difficulty is `hard`, not `expected-wall`.
